sense: of a person: obliging, ready to help

terms.gloss: obliging, ready to be of service
terms.comment: From officium, a kind service: ready to do people a good turn, especially those one owes respect to (Lewis & Short).

evidence: Ter. Hec. 5.3.39: benignō et lepidō et cōmī
terms.comment: Friendly and easy to deal with; more about manner than service.

phrases.latin: cōmēs, benignī, facilēs, suāvēs hominēs esse dīcuntur quī errantī cōmiter mōnstrant viam
phrases.english: people are called kind, generous, obliging and pleasant who show a man who has lost his way the road in a friendly manner

phrases.latin: estne quisquam quī tibi officiōsior līberāliorque videātur?
phrases.english: is there anyone who seems to you more obliging and generous?

sources: Lewis & Short: officiosus · Lewis & Short: comis
Cicero and Terence quoted as Lewis & Short quotes them.
John C. Traupman, Conversational Latin for Oral Proficiency, each phrase checked against the searchable text of the book.
